key_insight: Intra-patient 3D multimodal deformable registration remains unsolved across anatomies, with methods that improve overlap often failing to preserve global multimodal correspondence.
engineering_relevance: For clinical imaging pipelines, this means registration choice should be driven by the target anatomy and evaluated with both geometric and modality-aware metrics, not Dice alone.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based registration methods, including recent deep learning and foundation models.
Tested on three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical scenarios.
Evaluated with complementary metrics: DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC.
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans three datasets and shows strong performance variability, with learning-based methods winning on large synthetic cases but only limited gains in real pelvic registration.
watch_item: High overlap scores can be misleading because anatomy-guided methods may degrade outside segmented regions and geometric metrics can disagree with image-based similarity.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
